one_liner: MongoDB Atlas Administration API is a broad REST API with free self-serve service accounts (OAuth client-credentials, recommended) and legacy digest API keys; user-delegated OAuth is invite-only; official MCP exists.
auth_notes: Docs say service accounts (OAuth 2.0 client credentials) are recommended and HTTP Digest API keys are legacy. Authorization-code OAuth (delegated) is invite-only per a partner quickstart, so multi-user delegated OAuth is not self-serve; per-customer service accounts or keys work. Client-credentials-only OAuth arguably should not make OAUTH2 primary, but it is the documented main method for this API.
access_notes: Free Atlas account; Organization Owner can create service accounts or API keys. Free M0 cluster available. Admin API does not expose cluster data.
blocker_notes: Self-serve credentials available today. Delegated OAuth is invite-only, but per-customer service accounts/API keys work.

evidence.quote: The MongoDB Atlas Administration API allows developers to manage all components in MongoDB Atlas.
Atlas Administration API resources add, edit, or delete administrative objects within Atlas, including projects, users, and clusters.
The Atlas Administration API supports OAuth2 Service Accounts and HTTP Digest-based API keys. Service accounts are the recommended authentication method and API keys are considered a legacy option.
MongoDB Atlas OAuth is currently **invite-only**. Client credentials are **not self-provisioned** — MongoDB provisions them manually on your behalf.

To create a service account or API keys for an organization, you must have [`Organization Owner`](https://mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles/#mongodb-authrole-Organization-Owner) access to that organization.
Free cluster (`M0`) | No cost | Learning MongoDB, prototyping, and other workloads that fit within the Atlas Free Cluster Limits.
A Model Context Protocol server for interacting with MongoDB Databases and MongoDB Atlas.
MongoDB Atlas Managed MCP Server, which MongoDB hosts and manages for you in Atlas.
